title: The 1958 concert recording and Billie Holiday's appearance
summary: She sang 'Loch Lomond' and 'I'm Beginning to See the Light' on the 'Seven Ages of Jazz' album and recalls a sick Billie doing 'Lover Man'.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Fortunately, before we entered this long lapse of any output from you, we are fortunate in that -- two sides that you performed in a concert in 1958 are available, although they're not -- it's a deleted albums, I should say, at the time that we're recording this. But I was able to find a copy of the album. And I'm delighted that I did. This is a concert you did in Connecticut.
Yes.
Your first live recording.
That's right.
I didn't even know that this was out as a recording. I really didn't. I see that the two selections on there,

"Loch Lomond" and I'm Beginning To See The Light -- on that particular concert, this is another one of Leonard Feather's productions.
We did a series of three outdoor concerts. And he had a quite a line-up there.
The title, perhaps I should add, is the "Seven Ages of Jazz." That's the title of the album.
Well, I've never seen the album. In fact, I didn't even know it had been put out as an album.
But I would like to explain why I'm doing "I'm Beginning To See The Light" in this album.
At the time we did the concert, Leonard had suggested --
Well I mean, since he couldn't get all the vocalists on the bill, I was supposed to sing the songs that identified with certain singers.
I did "Lover Come Back To Me" which was associated with Mildred Bailey; and "I'm Beginning To See The Light" which would be associated with Ella Fitzgerald.

And I did Lover Man which is associated with Billie Holiday.
And for the first couple of concerts, everything went along pretty well until Billie found out that I was doing Lover Man.
And I think that Billie probably got up out of her sick bed to come and do her own Lover Man.
And I recalled the concert in which Billie showed up to do the vocal on this. In fact, this was the one and only time that I'd ever been that close to Billie -- that is, on a conversational basis.
We had passed each other at different times and different clubs; but to have an opportunity to talk with each other, this was the first time.
We were on the same plane or bus or whatever we took to get to this theater.
(Inaudible)
This was another theater.
Wallingford, Connecticut.
Well this was Wallingford,

but I don't know whether that was the same concert in which she appeared.
But anyway, we sat next to each other on the plane. And she didn't show any signs of bitterness as to my having been chosen to do 'Lover Man.'
But it was pretty obvious that she was determined to do her own 'Lover Man.'
And I recalled she was just superb that night. She wasn't well, but she sang 'Lover Man' and she --
One other song.
Yeah, well she had to do more. She did more than one song, I'm sure, because it was a long concert.
Just what they put out on the album, I'm not sure.

But I do know that she showed up and she did her own 'Lover Man' which was superb. I mean, I wasn't trying to imitate Billie or Ella or Mildred, but was just chosen to represent those singers in that particular theme, The Seven Ages of Jazz.

And I was sort of glad she did show up, because I don't think anybody could do 'Lover Man' like Billie Holiday. Oh boy.
Well, we were fortunate enough to have the two songs that Leonard Feather decided to put on the album, and the tune by you.
Yeah. I'd like to hear it. I don't have it myself. But one of these days I'll get a chance to hear it.
Well I believed I took them down on tape at the same time I was recording your two songs from there. So I'll --
Yeah, one of these days we'll get together.
